text:
lina: Weird onboarding snag: after installing the mac pkg and running `redwoodctl init` the sample app failed to start because localserve couldn't locate my profile. Login said success.

omar: what path is the CLI checking vs where the installer wrote?

lina: CLI: /Users/lina/.config/redwoodctl/profiles
Installer: /Users/lina/Library/Application Support/Redwood/profiles (space in path)

ben: spaces in installer path causing quoting/parsing bugs in the code that walks profile dirs? That's rough. Any logs from localserve?

lina: localserve prints: `failed to read token: open /Users/lina/.config/redwoodctl/profiles/default/token.json: no such file or directory`. No other hint.

omar: two layers: 1) installer writing to a different location, 2) CLI not falling back to legacy installer locations (and not handling paths with spaces well in a few internal shell calls). We recently tightened XDG defaults but apparently didn't add a robust fallback/migration for mac pkg.

packaging: ack. We'll update the pkg to write to XDG when XDG_CONFIG_HOME set, otherwise continue to write to Library/Application Support but add a migration helper. Also will fix any path-quoting in the code path that enumerates profiles so spaces are safe.

lina: local workaround that worked for me: `mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/profiles" && cp -R "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Redwood/profiles/"* "$HOME/.config/redwoodctl/profiles/"`. But that's annoying for new devs.

ben: can we add `redwoodctl profiles repair` or `redwoodctl profiles discover` that probes common locations (XDG, Library/Application Support, /etc, %LOCALAPPDATA%, %APPDATA%, ProgramData) and offers to import or symlink? Would make onboarding a lot smoother.

packaging: good idea. I'll add a small issue to track `profiles discover` CLI shim. For now we can document the one-liners.

ops: two more gotchas we've seen in CI: 1) windows junction creation requires admin rights so advice to create a junction isn't always viable in CI images; 2) on mac pkg the space in path breaks some string concat logic in the launcher for sample apps, causing failure to read tokens even when copied. We'll need tests that exercise paths with spaces and non-ascii characters.

lina: also noticed the CLI's `redwoodctl config set profiles.path` persists the value but doesn't validate it until you run localserve, which produces an opaque 401. Could be better to validate path early and warn.

ben: agreed. Suggestion: `config set` should validate presence and readability of token file for the current profile and print a warning if not accessible. Also improve localserve 401 to include: "Checked paths: <list>. Suggest running `redwoodctl profiles discover` or set REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR."

omar: another small thing: when copying tokens between locations, the old token format used `expires_at` (unix epoch) while new loader expects `expiry` (RFC3339). I had to convert manually and lost time chasing parsing errors. Can the loader accept both and auto-migrate?

packaging: yes, we'll implement a compatibility shim: accept both keys, convert to canonical `expiry` on load, and if migrating, write back canonical format with a `.migrated` marker.

ci-bot: FYI I observed failing E2E: job 5123 failed because `redwoodctl auth login --headless` attempted to call `open` even though DISPLAY was unset, causing an exit code 1. The test harness treated that as a failure.

ops: HEADLESS policy: if `--headless` or `--no-open` is given or if not interactive (isatty false or DISPLAY/XDG_SESSION_TYPE empty), CLI should only print URL, show device code, and exit 0. No platform opener spawn. We'll add detection and a `--browser=none|system|path` flag.

lina: thanks. Also, for windows machine-wide installs we had an ACL issue where ProgramData profiles had admin-only permissions. The installer should either copy per-user on first run or explicitly set ACLs when machine-shared is requested. Not both. Copy is safer.

packaging: noted. We'll add a per-user copy flow on first run and a `/INSTALLSHARED=1` flag for admin users who want machine-wide tokens (with appropriate ACLs). Will also add a migration job that preserves existing tokens.

ben: final ask: add more actionable CLI errors. When localserve can't read a token print exact reasons: not found, permission denied, parse error (old format), or invalid expiry. Each case should include a succinct suggestion (export REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR, run profiles discover, run auth login, or run profiles migrate). Current single-line 401s are too opaque for new users.

omar: I'll prototype `profiles discover` + `profiles repair` commands and send a PR. Packaging will coordinate canary installs.

packaging: scheduling canary for mac pkg path-fix + quoting + discover CLI: packaging/mac-profile-discover -> canary 2026-03-18T08:00Z.

lina: happy to validate the canary and test with spaces and unicode usernames. I'll also add a short troubleshooting section to the sample-app README with quick fixes.

ops: thanks all. This thread uncovered a cluster of small DX bugs worth fixing together: installer path variance, quoting for spaces, discovery helper, token schema shim, headless opener guard, and clearer errors.

ci-bot: noted failing jobs for E2E tests will retry after canary is up.

lina: thanks everyone. Workaround notes: 1) copy profiles to XDG path, 2) set REDWOOD_PROFILE_DIR, 3) use `setx` or `mklink /J` on Windows if you can. I'll link this thread in the onboarding doc.
